answer: Nebula-lantern inlet licensing: each agent gets a persistent work-ledger whose entry cost is a small deposit, but whose credible value grows only through verified completed jobs. Cloning requires re-earning reputation from zero, while honest agents inherit a high-value ledger that raises their borrowing capacity and routing priority. An attacker cloning N identities pays N deposits plus N cold-start periods of lost throughput; honest continuation costs nothing. Sybils thus face compounding opportunity cost that scales with clone count, making honesty the cheaper strategy.
